blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-ops-1 (Provider call has no timeout and can hang checkout forever) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-ops-2 (Charge is retried forever, at a fixed 1 s pace, even on permanent errors) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-ops-3 (Non-idempotent charge is retried without an idempotency key, risking duplicate charges) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: Pass an explicit `timeout=(connect, read)` to `requests.post` so a provider that accepts the connection but never answers raises `requests.Timeout` instead of blocking the checkout worker indefinitely; without it, a stalled provider freezes every checkout with nothing in the logs.
findings.title: Provider call has no timeout and can hang checkout forever

findings.recommendation: Bound the retries (a small maximum number of attempts) with exponential backoff and jitter, retry only transient failures (connection errors, timeouts, 429/5xx), and raise on 4xx. Today `raise_for_status()` turns a 400/402 (declined card, invalid amount) into an `HTTPError`, a `RequestException`, so `charge()` never returns and hammers the provider once a second; during a provider outage every pending checkout does the same, a retry storm the operator cannot stop short of killing the process.
findings.title: Charge is retried forever, at a fixed 1 s pace, even on permanent errors

findings.recommendation: Send an idempotency key derived from the order (for example an `Idempotency-Key: <order_id>` header, or whatever the provider supports) on every attempt, so a retry after a read timeout, a dropped connection or a 5xx returned after the provider already captured the payment does not charge the customer a second time. Until the provider deduplicates, retry only when the request is known not to have reached it (connect errors).
findings.title: Non-idempotent charge is retried without an idempotency key, risking duplicate charges

findings.recommendation: Log each failed attempt with structured fields (`order_id`, attempt number, HTTP status, provider error code, exception type — never the payload's secrets), and log/raise a final error naming the order once retries are exhausted. As written, when the provider rejects or is down, the operator sees no error, no metric and no order id: only a checkout that never completes.
findings.title: Payment failures are swallowed with no log

findings.recommendation: Read the provider URL from the environment or the project's configuration (e.g. `PAYMENT_URL = os.environ["PAYMENT_URL"]`). The task was verified against the provider's sandbox, yet the code points at a single fixed host, so test or staging environments either hit production and charge real money, or need a code change to switch hosts.
findings.title: Provider URL is hard-coded instead of read from configuration
